title: Calendar Year 2027 Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) Proposed Rule (CMS-1850-P)
date_evidence: Fact Sheets Jul 02, 2026 - Calendar Year 2027 Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) Proposed Rule (CMS-1850-P)
key_claim: CMS proposes to extend its off-campus volume-control method to imaging without contrast, paying the Physician Fee Schedule equivalent rate, after applying the same method to clinic visits in CY 2019 and drug administration in CY 2026; the step is estimated to cut Part B spending by about $260 million and beneficiary cost sharing by about $70 million in year one, and CMS also proposes to remove 638 services from the inpatient-only list and to pay 340B drugs at ASP minus 33.4%.
frame_summary: This source argues that Medicare should pay the same rate for the same outpatient service regardless of the setting, and presents each annual expansion as one more application of an existing statutory volume-control method.
verbatim_quote: For CY 2027, CMS is proposing to include imaging without contrast services furnished in excepted off-campus PBDs.
verbatim_list: In the CY 2026 OPPS/ASC final rule, CMS finalized a policy expansion to include drug administration services furnished in excepted off-campus PBDs.

In the CY 2019 OPPS/ASC final rule, CMS adopted a method to control unnecessary increases in the volume of the clinic visit services furnished in excepted off-campus provider-based departments (PBDs).

we estimate this provision would reduce Medicare Part B expenditures by approximately $260 million in the first year, including approximately $190 million in Part B savings and approximately $70 million in reduced beneficiary premiums
we are proposing for CY 2027 to pay for 340B acquired drugs at the drug's Average Sales Price (ASP) minus 33.4%.
This proposal is estimated to reduce Original Medicare drug payment by $4.55 billion dollars and beneficiary drug payments by $1.15 billion in the first year.
CMS is proposing to remove 638 services from the following clinical families
CMS is proposing to revise the annual offset percentage for non-drug items and services from 0.5% to 3% effective CY 2027
These proposed payment policies would affect approximately 3,500 hospitals and approximately 6,400 ASCs.
CMS proposes updating OPPS payment rates for hospitals that meet applicable quality reporting requirements by 2.4%.

title: CMS Acts to Strengthen Care Quality, Cut Drug Costs, and Slash Out-of-Pocket Expenses for Medicare Beneficiaries
date_evidence: Press Releases Jul 02, 2026 - CMS Acts to Strengthen Care Quality, Cut Drug Costs, and Slash Out-of-Pocket Expenses for Medicare Beneficiaries
key_claim: CMS states that site-of-care payment differentials can push services into higher-cost settings and may encourage consolidation by motivating hospitals to acquire independent physician practices to raise their Medicare prices, and frames the CY 2027 rule as removing those disparities.
frame_summary: This source argues that the outpatient payment differential is itself a driver of hospital acquisition of physician practices, and that removing it is an affordability measure rather than a cut.
verbatim_quote: Such payment differentials can encourage health systems to shift services to higher-cost settings without a clinical need for doing so and may encourage greater consolidation within the healthcare system by motivating hospitals to acquire independent physician practices to increase their Medicare prices.
verbatim_list: removing site-of-care disparities that have unnecessarily driven up costs for millions of seniors
for total reduced drugs spending of approximately $5.7 billion in 2027 alone

notes: The agency's own statement of intent, which is the load-bearing evidence that the consolidation effect is the target rather than a side effect. Quote verified by hand against the live page during the 20/09/2026 sourcing pass.

title: CMS Proposes Major CY 2027 OPPS/ASC Changes Targeting 340B Payments, Site-Neutral Policy, IPO List Phase-Out, and ASC Expansion
key_claim: The inpatient-only list held about 1,428 services, 285 were removed in CY 2026 and 637 are proposed for CY 2027, with full elimination due by 1 January 2029; about 618 surgical codes would join the ASC covered procedures list; the 340B survey drew usable responses from about 41% of eligible hospitals and found 340B drugs acquired 33.4% below ASP against non-340B drugs at 2.7% above; total CY 2027 OPPS payments are projected at about $110.9 billion.
frame_summary: This source argues that the CY 2027 rule is best read as a coordinated package moving surgical and outpatient volume out of hospital settings while repricing what remains, rather than as a set of separate annual adjustments.
verbatim_quote: For CY 2027, CMS continues to phase out the IPO list by proposing to remove an additional 637 services.
verbatim_list: The current list includes about 1,428 services.
The phase-out began on January 1, 2026, with the removal of 285 services.
In CY 2026, CMS proposed to phase out the IPO list entirely over a three-year time period, with full elimination by January 1, 2029.
For CY 2027, CMS proposes adding approximately 618 surgery or surgery-like codes

Based on usable survey responses from approximately 41 percent of eligible hospitals, CMS found that hospitals acquired non-340B drugs at prices 2.7 percent above ASP, while 340B drugs were acquired at prices 33.4 percent below ASP.
are expected to reach approximately $110.9 billion, an increase of approximately $9.5 billion compared to estimated CY 2026 OPPS payments
CMS also estimates that the proposed 340B remedy offset would reduce payments to affected providers by $2.3 billion in CY 2027.

key_claim: Responding to CMS's request for comment on further services, the American Action Forum nominates five more service families covering 20 APCs and estimates savings above $1.6 billion in the first nine months of CY 2027 plus about $410 million in beneficiary coinsurance, noting claims data showing provider-based departments received about 320% more than physician offices for the same level 1 skin procedure.
frame_summary: This source argues that site neutrality should be treated as a general payment principle to be applied across service families rather than as a series of isolated annual adjustments.

title: CMS' 2027 outpatient pay proposal brings 340B, site-neutral changes, to hospitals' dismay
key_claim: Hospital groups attacked the proposal immediately, with 340B Health arguing the cut redistributes revenue to non-safety-net providers and America's Essential Hospitals calling the site-neutral step another cut hospitals need to stay open, while CMS wrote that for most 340B providers the reduced drug payments will outweigh the increased non-drug payments.
frame_summary: This source argues that the rule sets a federal cost-control agenda against a hospital sector that regards the same measures as a threat to service viability, and reports the collision rather than adjudicating it.
verbatim_quote: yet another cut to Medicare payments that hospitals desperately need to stay open and serve their communities
verbatim_list: instead uses that revenue to pay more to non-safety net providers
for most 340B providers, the decreased 340B drug payments will outweigh the increased payments for non-drug services
the agency wrote in the proposed rule that
said the change would head off health systems' consolidation incentives in order to deliver their care in higher cost settings
Combining the proposed rate with other policies being floated by the agency would result in an overall 1.9% increase, or $1.8 billion, in total payments over the 2026 calendar year
notes: Quote attributed on the page to Jennifer DeCubellis, president and CEO of America's Essential Hospitals; the redistribution quote is attributed to Maureen Testoni of 340B Health. Quote verified by hand against the live page during the 20/09/2026 sourcing pass.

title: CMS CY 2027 OPPS/ASC Proposed Rule: Key Payment and Policy Changes for Hospitals, Health Systems, and ASCs
date_evidence: Date: 3 August 2026 US Healthcare and FDA Alert
key_claim: To implement section 6225 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, CMS proposes that from 1 January 2028 each off-campus hospital outpatient department bill under its own National Provider Identifier, with the main provider submitting a provider-based attestation demonstrating compliance with provider-based rules.
frame_summary: This source argues that the operational exposure in the rule sits with 340B participants and operators of off-campus provider-based departments, and that the new enrolment conditions are as consequential as the rate changes.
verbatim_quote: Each department would bill under its own National Provider Identifier, and the main provider would be required to submit a provider-based attestation demonstrating compliance with applicable provider-based rules.
verbatim_list: To implement Section 6225 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, CMS proposes new enrollment conditions for off-campus hospital outpatient departments beginning 1 January 2028.
Comments are due 31 August 2026, and CMS expects to publish a final rule later this year.

CMS continues to expand site-neutral payment policies, proposing to expand reduced payment rates to outpatient imaging services and moving forward with new enrollment requirements for off-campus hospital outpatient departments.
notes: Specialist healthcare regulatory alert. Quote verified by hand against the live page during the 20/09/2026 sourcing pass.

title: CMS Issues CY 2027 OPPS Proposed Rule
key_claim: The safety-net hospital association reads the 340B proposal as a total cut of 39.4% from the default OPPS rate of average sales price plus 6%, implemented budget neutrally with the savings reinvested in the conversion factor for non-drug items at all OPPS hospitals.
frame_summary: This source argues that the rule transfers resources away from safety-net hospitals to the wider hospital field without reducing what Medicare spends overall.
verbatim_quote: CMS proposes to cut outpatient drug reimbursement for hospitals participating in the 340B Drug Pricing Program by a total of 39.4% from the default OPPS payment rate for outpatient drugs of average sales price plus 6%.
verbatim_list: The cut would be implemented in a budget-neutral manner, with the savings reinvested in an increased conversion factor for non-drug items and services at all OPPS hospitals.
CMS now proposes to accelerate recoupment by cutting the conversion factor by 3% in 2027.
notes: Tier 4 advocacy source, used only for the counter-argument and for the sector's own framing of the 340B arithmetic. Its inpatient-only list figures differ from the CMS fact sheet (637 against 638 services, and CY 2028 against CY 2029 for full elimination); the CMS and Applied Policy figures are used in the body. Quote verified by hand against the live page during the 20/09/2026 sourcing pass.
